sources.finding: set_num_threads writes process atomic desired count and current OpenMP/MKL thread settings. init_num_threads reapplies stored count; get_num_threads lazily initializes each calling thread. set_num_threads also clears MKLDNN forward convolution computation cache.
lazy_init_num_threads uses thread_local initialized flag, calls init_num_threads once for each calling thread.
clear_computation_cache clears ideep convolution_forward t_store because it caches maximum OpenMP workers.
Documented to set CPU intra-op parallelism; call before eager/JIT/autograd execution.

conclusion: Worker-context thread qualification is incomplete in first WAN attempt. PyTorch2.8 OpenMP desired count is process-global but native OpenMP/MKL limits are applied to the current thread; per-thread lazy initialization need not occur before every backend entry. Separate same-version x86 native probe observes a fresh Python thread at OpenMP24/MKL24 before and after a torch.mm call despite main set_num_threads(1); calling worker get_num_threads then initializes both to1. Explicit worker set_num_threads(1) before any execution produces1 throughout. This establishes a reproducible initialization gap and invalidates an unconditional worker-thread1 guarantee, but does not prove the actual ASR/vision model used more than1 throughout or explain its observed latency change. Live task counts include other libraries and idle threads; sampled task-time deltas were almost entirely zero. First attempt must remain separate and labelled thread qualification incomplete; initialize and record settings in actual serving worker before any job, then fresh calibration/redeployment/evaluation.

local_native_probe.scope: Separate host process, PyTorch2.8.0+cpu, synthetic512x512 mm only. No model execution or target-process modification. Native API calls avoid initializing Torch thread context while observing it.

initial_probe_caveat: worker torch.get_num_threads() itself calls lazy_init_num_threads and changes native OpenMP/MKL context, so its result1 cannot establish that earlier target-worker operators used1.

sequence: Adapter/model loaded in main with interop setting unchanged.

Inside the persistent serving thread before reading any job: torch.set_num_threads(1); read torch.get_num_threads() and torch.get_num_interop_threads(); assert both1; record threading.get_native_id(), initialization UTC, Torchversion, effective values.
Publish worker-ready only after this completes; attach resulting metadata to health and receipts. Do not set_num_threads on each request because source shows it clears the MKLDNN computation cache.
Each request can record/check native worker identity; optional native libgomp/mkl calls are platform-specific corroboration, not portable requirement.
New run starts with fresh calibration. Preserve first attempt and do not pool old/new implementation latency.
